title: Could the Iran war last another year?
credits: Photos: Unsplash (Tehran, file) · Map: Natural Earth
lines: America's ambassador to the United Nations says the war with Iran could last another year.
Mike Waltz told the Financial Times that the US would not meet its key goals until Iran gives up its highly enriched uranium.
He said the US Navy could keep up its blockade of Iranian ports for the foreseeable future.
President Trump says any new strikes would wait until after the US midterm elections on the third of November.
Iran's army chief says US warships will never be allowed into the Persian Gulf, under any circumstances.
Oil markets are nervous. Brent crude rose above one hundred and seventeen dollars a barrel on Friday, its highest since March.
At the start of October, it was below ninety-seven dollars.
The US State Department is also reducing staff at embassies in Jordan, Lebanon, Qatar and the UAE.
But there is still a diplomatic door. Iran's ambassador to Pakistan says Tehran remains open to talks under the Pakistan-brokered interim deal agreed in June.
And in Istanbul, European and Middle Eastern ministers urged restraint, warning that escalation would leave no winners.
For Pakistan, which imports most of its oil, a long war means a long period of high fuel prices.
